citation.authors: Thondre PS, Young E, Pledger S, et al.
citation.title: A randomized controlled trial in healthy participants to compare the insulinogenic effects of whey protein and pea protein co-ingested with glucose

population.description: Thirty healthy, moderately active, non-smoking adults who completed all five test sessions (13 male, 17 female; Table 2, mean ± SD). Forty-four were recruited (aged 19 to 57 y, BMI <= 30, fasting glucose < 6.1 mmol/L, no diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance by health questionnaire); the 19 to 57 range is for the 44 recruited, so min and max are left null.

protocols.name: glu_50g
protocols.description: Reference: 50 g glucose (Table 1: 50 g available carbohydrate, no protein, fat or fibre) dissolved in 250 ml water, drunk over 15 min from minute 0 (entered as one meal at minute 0). After a 12-hour overnight fast; sessions started before 10:00 (clock hour not stated, 8.0 entered); capillary samples to 180 min, so 181 minutes are simulated. Minute 0 is the start of drinking.

After a 12-hour overnight fast; sessions started before 10:00 (clock hour not stated, 8.0 entered); capillary samples to 180 min, so 181 minutes are simulated. Minute 0 is the start of drinking.

protocols.name: glu_50g_runin
protocols.description: Reference: 50 g glucose (Table 1: 50 g available carbohydrate, no protein, fat or fibre) dissolved in 250 ml water, drunk over 15 min from arm minute 5 (entered as one meal at minute 5). After a 12-hour overnight fast; sessions started before 10:00 (clock hour not stated, 8.0 entered); capillary baseline samples at -5 and 0 min before drinking, then samples to 180 min after the start of drinking: arm minute 0 is the paper's -5 min, so the drink is at arm minute 5 and 186 minutes are simulated. Used only for the glucose incremental area, whose baseline the paper defines as the mean of the -5 and 0 min samples.

findings.description: Capillary blood glucose incremental area 0-180 min after GLU; trapezoid rule over the samples at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180 min after the start of drinking (arm minutes 5 to 185). Baseline is the mean of the -5 and 0 min samples (Methods 2.5), the baseline window of the run-in. The paper does not say what happens below baseline. Only the whole 180 min area is entered (Table 3 also prints 60, 90, 120 min areas of the same curve).

Plasma insulin incremental area 0-180 min after GLU; trapezoid rule over the samples at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180 min. The paper states a baseline (mean of -5 and 0 min) only for blood glucose; insulin was also sampled at -5 min but its baseline is not defined, so the 0 min sample is used. The paper does not say what happens below baseline. Only the whole 180 min area is entered.
